You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

## The drawn closing-era filing (what the accession actually reports)
- The drawn filing is a Form 8-K under Item 2.02 (Results of Operations and Financial Condition): on May 2, 2018 Compass Diversified Holdings and Compass Group Diversified Holdings LLC (NYSE: CODI) issued a press release announcing consolidated operating results for the three months ended March 31, 2018. It is an earnings release, not a deal-terms document. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Item 2.02]
- That release records that during the first quarter of 2018 CODI "Consummated the accretive platform acquisition of Foam Fabricators, Inc." and "Consummated the add-on acquisition of Rimports Inc. by CODI's subsidiary Sterno Products, LLC." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press release]
- The release describes CODI as "an owner of leading middle market businesses" that "maintains controlling ownership interests in each of its subsidiaries," provides "both debt and equity capital for its subsidiaries," and lists ten majority-owned operating subsidiaries across distinct lines of business (5.11, Advanced Circuits, Arnold Magnetic Technologies, Clean Earth, Crosman, Ergobaby, Foam Fabricators, Liberty Safe, Manitoba Harvest, Sterno Products). [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press release]
- Closing-era balance-sheet effect of the quarter's acquisitions: goodwill and intangible assets, net rose from $1,112,206 thousand at December 31, 2017 to $1,415,898 thousand at March 31, 2018; net cash used in investing activities for the quarter was $415,628 thousand. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Exhibit 99.1 condensed consolidated financial statements]

## Platform acquisition — Foam Fabricators (deal structure at closing)
- On February 15, 2018, FFI Compass, Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company ("Acquisition Sub"), acquired all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of Foam Fabricators, Inc. pursuant to a Stock Purchase Agreement dated January 18, 2018 between Acquisition Sub and Warren F. Florkiewicz; Foam Fabricators became a wholly owned subsidiary of Acquisition Sub and an indirect subsidiary of the Company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- The Company paid a purchase price of approximately $247.5 million, before working-capital and other adjustments, funded through a draw on its revolving credit facility; the Company's initial equity ownership in Acquisition Sub was approximately 100% on a primary and 92% on a fully diluted basis. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- Concurrent with closing, the Company (as lender) provided an intercompany credit facility to Foam Fabricators and its wholly owned subsidiary Foam Fab, Inc. (the "Foam Fab Credit Agreement"), with approximately $115.0 million outstanding on the closing date, secured by substantially all assets of the guarantors and by pledges of the equity interests in Foam Fabricators and Foam Fab; the Company noted the terms were "similar to the terms and conditions of the credit facilities in place with its existing subsidiary businesses." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- The customer-facing business acquired: Foam Fabricators is "a leading designer and manufacturer of custom molded protective foam solutions and OEM components made from expanded polymers such as expanded polystyrene (EPS) and expanded polypropylene (EPP)," headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, operating 13 molding and fabricating facilities across North America, serving appliances/electronics, pharmaceuticals, health-and-wellness, automotive and building-products end-markets, with trailing-twelve-months (ended Nov 30, 2017) net revenue of approximately $126 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017 Subsequent Events]

## Add-on acquisition — Rimports (deal structure at closing)
- On February 26, 2018, CODI's existing portfolio company Sterno Products, LLC acquired all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of Rimports, Inc. (a Utah corporation) under a Stock Purchase Agreement dated January 23, 2018 with Jeffery W. Palmer and affiliated family trusts; Rimports became a wholly owned subsidiary of Sterno and an indirect subsidiary of the Company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000011, 8-K Item 8.01]
- Sterno paid a purchase price of approximately $145 million (excluding working-capital adjustments and a potential earn-out of up to $25 million based on future financial performance), funded through a draw on the Company's revolving credit facility; the acquisition was folded into Sterno's existing October 10, 2014 intercompany credit and guarantee/collateral arrangements by amendment (additional term loans of $136.0 million and revolving loans of $10.0 million), with Rimports joined as a guarantor. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000011, 8-K Item 8.01]
- The filing frames this explicitly as consolidation under an existing platform: "The following description relates to the recent add-on acquisition of a business by one of CODI's existing portfolio companies, Sterno." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000011, 8-K Item 8.01]

## Holding-company / roll-up structure at the closing era (contemporaneous annual report)
- The registrant and the Trust (collectively "CODI") "were formed to acquire and manage a group of small and middle-market businesses headquartered in North America"; the Company states "We acquire controlling interests in and actively manage businesses." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017]
- The vehicle is externally managed: day-to-day operations and affairs of the Company are managed by Compass Group Management LLC ("CGM" or "our Manager") under a Management Services Agreement; the Company "pay[s] our Manager a quarterly management fee," which "covers all expenses related to the services performed by our Manager, including the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and other personnel." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017]
- Acquired businesses are run on a decentralized basis with their own management retained: the Company states "we operate our businesses on a stand-alone basis, primarily relying on existing management teams for management of their day-to-day operations," while noting that "opportunities exist to augment existing management at such businesses." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017]
- As of December 31, 2017 the Company held controlling interests in a portfolio of separately operated businesses (e.g., it "made loans to and purchased a controlling interest in" Crosman on June 2, 2017 for approximately $150 million), each described as maintaining its own management team and market niche. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017]

## Structural summary (closing era only)
- The drawn accession is an Item 2.02 earnings release reporting Q1-2018 results; the transactions it records are the platform acquisition of Foam Fabricators (a controlling stock purchase into a newly formed Acquisition Sub, ~$247.5 million, closed Feb 15, 2018) and the add-on acquisition of Rimports by existing subsidiary Sterno (~$145 million + up to $25 million earn-out, closed Feb 26, 2018). [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Exhibit 99.1] [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01] [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000011, 8-K Item 8.01]
- Both are structured as whole-stock purchases that bring the customer-facing product operations (and, per the annual report, their existing management teams and stand-alone operating processes) under CODI's controlling ownership, financed through the parent's revolving facility and intercompany credit agreements, within an externally managed holding structure that leaves acquired businesses to run on a stand-alone basis under CGM oversight. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017] [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]

[SLICE END]

## Platform acquisition — Foam Fabricators (deal structure at closing)
- On February 15, 2018, FFI Compass, Inc., a Delaware corporation and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company ("Acquisition Sub"), acquired all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of Foam Fabricators, Inc. pursuant to a Stock Purchase Agreement dated January 18, 2018 between Acquisition Sub and Warren F. Florkiewicz; Foam Fabricators became a wholly owned subsidiary of Acquisition Sub and an indirect subsidiary of the Company. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- The Company paid a purchase price of approximately $247.5 million, before working-capital and other adjustments, funded through a draw on its revolving credit facility; the Company's initial equity ownership in Acquisition Sub was approximately 100% on a primary and 92% on a fully diluted basis. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- Concurrent with closing, the Company (as lender) provided an intercompany credit facility to Foam Fabricators and its wholly owned subsidiary Foam Fab, Inc. (the "Foam Fab Credit Agreement"), with approximately $115.0 million outstanding on the closing date, secured by substantially all assets of the guarantors and by pledges of the equity interests in Foam Fabricators and Foam Fab; the Company noted the terms were "similar to the terms and conditions of the credit facilities in place with its existing subsidiary businesses." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01]
- The customer-facing business acquired: Foam Fabricators is "a leading designer and manufacturer of custom molded protective foam solutions and OEM components made from expanded polymers such as expanded polystyrene (EPS) and expanded polypropylene (EPP)," headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, operating 13 molding and fabricating facilities across North America, serving appliances/electronics, pharmaceuticals, health-and-wellness, automotive and building-products end-markets, with trailing-twelve-months (ended Nov 30, 2017) net revenue of approximately $126 million. [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017 Subsequent Events]

- The registrant and the Trust (collectively "CODI") "were formed to acquire and manage a group of small and middle-market businesses headquartered in North America"; the Company states "We acquire controlling interests in and actively manage businesses." - The vehicle is externally managed: day-to-day operations and affairs of the Company are managed by Compass Group Management LLC ("CGM" or "our Manager") under a Management Services Agreement; the Company "pay[s] our Manager a quarterly management fee," which "covers all expenses related to the services performed by our Manager, including the compensation of our Chief Executive Officer and other personnel." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000014, 10-K FY2017]
- Acquired businesses are run on a decentralized basis with their own management retained: the Company states "we operate our businesses on a stand-alone basis, primarily relying on existing management teams for management of their day-to-day operations," while noting that "opportunities exist to augment existing management at such businesses." [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000037, 8-K Exhibit 99.1] [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000009, 8-K Item 8.01] [SRC: SEC accession 0001345126-18-000011, 8-K Item 8.01]
